questions.prompt: For a plane-polarised electromagnetic wave, state what is restricted to one direction and name the line on a polarising filter that shows the allowed direction.
Plane-polarised light meets a filter whose transmission axis is aligned with its plane of polarisation. What is the transmitted intensity?
A filter axis is at 60 degrees to the incident plane of polarisation. Which fraction of the incident intensity is transmitted?
Light leaves filter P polarised along P's axis. It then reaches filter Q. Which angle belongs in Malus's law for filter Q?

options.A: the angle between the original plane and Q
options.B: the angle between the axes of P and Q
options.C: the angle through which P was rotated
options.D: twice the angle between P and Q

figure.purpose: Assess angle tracking through an original two-filter sequence.
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white sequence. Show a vertical incident-polarisation arrow, filter R axis at 30 degrees to vertical, and filter S axis at 70 degrees to vertical. Label axes and angles but include no inter-filter angle, intensity or amplitude answers.
figure.alt_text: A vertical plane-polarised beam passes through axes at 30 and 70 degrees to vertical.
